chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Hamzah, from Abu Ishaq, from one of the companions of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: Know that the companionship of the scholar and following him is a religion by which Allah is worshipped, and obedience to him is a means of acquiring good deeds, an effacer of evil deeds, a ذخيرة for the believers, an elevation among them in their lifetime, and a beauty after their death.

key_terms.الْعَالِمِ: the scholar, one possessing authoritative religious knowledge
key_terms.دِينٌ: a matter of religion and devotion to Allah
key_terms.ذَخِيرَةٌ: a stored provision or treasure for benefit
key_terms.مَكْسَبَةٌ لِلْحَسَنَاتِ: a cause of earning good deeds
key_terms.مَمْحَاةٌ لِلسَّيِّئَاتِ: that which wipes away evil deeds
key_terms.وَاتِّبَاعَهُ: following him in belief and conduct

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam Ali عليه السلام emphasize companionship with and obedience to the true scholar?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that keeping the company of the true scholar and following him is part of the religion through which Allah is obeyed. Obedience to such divinely guided authority brings spiritual benefit, erases sins, elevates the believers in life, and leaves them with a noble remembrance after death.
